Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 48 s. 2023 JUL 2) 'zoa MR. YON VILLEGAS Yon.styx@gmail.com Dear Villegas: This has reference to your electronic mail dated June 7, 2023 requesting for clarification on the designation of a municipal accountant — spouse of the incumbent Mayor. At the outset, this Department deems it imperative to determine whether the law on nepotism is applicable in the case at hand. However, before answering the same, we should first determine whether an Accountant is a Career Service or Non-Career Service position as Section 79 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) states: SECTION 79. Limitation on Appointment. — No person shall be appointed in the career service of the local government if he is related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to the appointing or recommending authority. (Emphasis ours) Career Service shall be characterized by (1) entrance based on merit and fitness to be determined as far as practicable by competitive examination, or based on highly technical qualifications; (2) opportunity for advancement to higher career positions; and (3) security of tenurel. One of the classes of positions in the Career Service to which requires examinations is the second level which includes professional, technical, and scientific positions which involve professional, technical, or scientific work in a non- supervisory or supervisory capacity requiring at least four years of college work up to Division Chief leve12. On the other hand, Non-Career Service shall be characterized by (1) entrance on bases other than those of the usual tests of merit and fitness utilized for the career service; and (2) tenure which is limited to a period specified by law, or which is coterminous with that of the appointing authority or subject to his pleasure, or which is limited to the duration of a particular project for which purpose employment was made. It shall include elective officials and their personal or confidential staff. Unlike the positions of Administrator, Information Officer and Legal Officer, which is coterminous (primarily confidential) with that of the local chief executive who appointed 1 Section 7, Chapter 2, Title l, Book V of the Administrative Code of 1987 2 Section 8(b), Chapter 2, Title I, Book V of the Administrative Code of 1987 3 Section 9, Title l, Book V of the Administrative Code of 198 Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

them4, Accountants belong to the Career Service position because of the eligibility requirement under the Local Government Code, specifically Section 474 thereof, viz: SECTION. 474. Qualifications, Powers and Dut,es . - (a) No person shall be appointed accountant unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, and a certified public accountant. He must have acquired experience in the treasury or accounting service for at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial or city accountant, and three (3) years in the case of the municipal accountant. The appointment of an accountant is mandatory for the provincial, city and municipal governments. Xxx (Emphasis supplied) It may be well to note that the Civil Service Commission (CSC) in its Resolution NO. 0301285 has ratiocinated that: From the above, it is clear that the position of Administrator is coterminous with the term of the appointing authority and highly confidential in nature. However, it is a unique position because while it is highly confidential in character, it is required that the appointee must meet the qualifications enumerated under Section 480 of the Local Government Code. Hence, the position of Administrator does not fall within the confidential/personal staff contemplated under Section I (e) of CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998 which dispenses with the eligibility and experience requirements. Considering that an Accountant is a Career Service position, we are of the view that the Mayor is prohibited to appoint/designate his/her spouse as the Accountant of the Municipality as it violates the law on nepotism which has been defined by the Civil Service Law as bestowal of patronage by public officers in appointing others to positions by reason of blood or marital relationship to the appointing authority6. On a note, the Supreme Court in the case of Jose P. Laurel vs. Civil Service Commission7 has ruled that appointment should not be differentiated from designation. Career Service may be filled up only by appointment, either permanent or temporary; hence, a designation of a person to fill it up because it is vacancy is necessarily included in the term appointment, for it precisely accomplishes the same purpose. Moreover, if a designation is not to deemed included in the term appointment under Section 49 of Presidential Decree No. 8078, then the prohibition on nepotism would be meaningless and toothless. Any appointing authority may circumvent it by merely designating, and not appointing, a relative within the prohibited degree to a vacant position in the career service. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly.
